shipped_rows.title_o: Revisiting the Investment Theory of Creativity
shipped_rows.outcome_quote: The present data not only confirmed the theory-practice and gender discrepancies previously found among mainland Chinese university students

parent_scope_objection: Second and final scoped scientific review, one prior scientific opinion retained in the attempt ceiling. Do not repair the legacy normalized/nonliteral quote or assume a technical inspector has decided correctness. Independent raw primary inspection raised this precise unresolved question: Legacy scientific decision and raw provider wording are preserved, but its nonliteral proof has not yet passed new literal-primary/context inspection. The local girls/boys contrast is real, but the later author conclusion says the study largely replicated the findings, particularly theory–practice and gender gaps. The claimed absence of a governing broad verdict needs scientific resolution. Read the full original-specific Results/Discussion/Conclusion, all earlier source/argument history and codebook. Settle the actual finding/type/identity and any dependent outcome using a short contiguous raw literal passage; distinct passages may be separately recorded, never spliced. The author whole-target synthesis governs over a secondary contrast, but generic theory or other-original support cannot be transferred. Same-source access is not identical sample/data; computational rerun, alternative-specification robustness and new-sample tests must remain separate. If there is an actual primary-source ambiguity or evidence-access limit, identify it exactly; no forced verdict. If original/type remains unresolved, do not transfer a categorical outcome. A removal needs positive target/duplicate evidence, never title/DOI difference alone.

prior_scientific_decisions.quote: In Zhang and Sternberg’s study, the mainland research participants rated intellectual styles as the most important resource for crea- tivity in their explicit evaluation of the six resources, while they indicated that intel- lectual styles would be the second most important resource when they evaluated the hypothetical cases. However, in the present study, whereas the Hong Kong partici- pants’ratings of boys were consistent with those in Zhang and Sternberg’s study, their ratings of girls were not.
prior_scientific_decisions.reason: The study set out to test whether two major types of findings from Zhang and Sternberg (2011a) replicated: (a) theory-practice discrepancies centred on intelligence and on intellectual styles, and (b) the gender gap in expectations. While the authors confirm the gender gap and find a smaller theory-practice gap on intelligence (stating later that the study 'largely replicated' the original findings), they explicitly contrast the girls' intellectual-style ratings in the hypothetical cases with Zhang and Sternberg (2011a), where intellectual style was the second most important resource across hypothetical cases but dropped to fourth/sixth for girls here. Under the codebook rules, when a tested finding is explicitly contrasted as differing from the original alongside other replicated findings, the outcome is 'mixed'.
